title: WiSE-OD
contribution: Weight-space ensembling for OOD RGB-T detection; introduces LLVIP-C / FLIR-C.
notes: Corruption-benchmark protocol (AP50, mPC) a reviewer may demand alignment with.

title: Infrared and Visible Image Fusion: From Data Compatibility to Task Adaption
contribution: Comprehensive IVIF survey organized around task adaptation.
notes: Authoritative section anchor from the TarDAL/M3FD group.

title: MSOD-Bench: Optimizing Multispectral Object Detection
contribution: Standardized re-implementation/benchmark of 20+ RGB-T detectors.
notes: Fair-comparison framing; guards against cherry-picked baseline numbers.

title: CDDFuse
contribution: Correlation-driven dual-branch decomposition fusion, incl. downstream detection.
notes: Task-coupled fusion line (fusion-for-detection).

title: MetaFusion
contribution: Detection-guided meta-feature embedding mutually promoting fusion and detection.
notes: Supports the manuscript's task-constrained motivation.

title: TarDAL: Target-aware Dual Adversarial Learning and a Multi-scenario Multi-Modality Benchmark to Fuse Infrared and Visible for Object Detection
contribution: Target-aware dual adversarial learning that fuses infrared and visible images for detection; introduced the M3FD benchmark.
notes: Classic task-coupled fusion entry; the M3FD dataset paper.

title: UniRGB-IR
contribution: Adapter injection of RGB-IR fusion into a frozen ViT foundation model.
notes: Foundation-model line; FLIR mAP 44.1 / LLVIP 63.2.

title: C2Former: Calibrated and Complementary Transformer
contribution: Cross-attention calibration + adaptive sampling for misaligned RGB-T pairs.
notes: Leading cross-attention line; note it does not evaluate on LLVIP/FLIR/M3FD.

title: DAMSDet
contribution: Competitive query selection + deformable cross-attention in a DETR RGB-T detector.
notes: SOTA DETR representative on M3FD/FLIR/LLVIP (FLIR mAP 49.3, LLVIP mAP 69.6).

title: GM-DETR
contribution: Lightweight DETR-style RGB-T detector.
notes: Additional DETR-line data point on FLIR + LLVIP.

title: ICAFusion: Iterative Cross-Attention Guided Feature Fusion for Multispectral Object Detection
contribution: Iterative cross-attention guided feature fusion for multispectral object detection.
notes: Established cross-attention fusion reference, widely used as a comparison baseline (LLVIP, M3FD).

title: Cross-Modality Fusion Transformer (CFT)
contribution: YOLOv5-based transformer cross-modal fusion for RGB-T detection.
notes: Canonical transformer-fusion baseline on FLIR + LLVIP; appears in all recent comparison tables.

title: YOLOv11-RGBT
contribution: Six-fusion-mode study over YOLO/RT-DETR with P3 mid-fusion + controllable fine-tuning (MCF).
notes: Direct predecessor: same backbone family and mid-fusion design point as the manuscript's detector.

title: DEYOLO
contribution: Dual semantic/spatial enhancement modules on YOLOv8 dual streams.
notes: YOLO-line comparator on M3FD + LLVIP.

title: LRAF-Net
contribution: Long-range attention fusion + complementary-mask augmentation vs single-modality bias.
notes: Bridges architecture and imbalance sections; FLIR/LLVIP results.

title: Fusion-Mamba
contribution: State-space (Mamba) cross-modal fusion for IR-VIS detection.
notes: Current SOTA-line representative (M3FD mAP 61.9 in comparative tables).

title: WaveMamba
contribution: Wavelet frequency-decomposed Mamba fusion with YOLOv8 head.
notes: Latest Mamba-line SOTA claim on M3FD/LLVIP/FLIR-Aligned.

title: Learning a Robust RGB-Thermal Detector for Extreme Modality Imbalance
contribution: Quality-mask interaction + pseudo-degradation + EMA base/auxiliary consistency for imbalanced RGB-T.
notes: **Closest prior work** — see §(b). KAIST LAMR + FLIR mAP; Gaussian-noise and contrast-degradation tests.

title: CALNet (Cross-Modal Conflict-Aware Learning)
contribution: Rectifies cross-modal feature conflict before selective fusion.
notes: "Conflict" framing is a conceptual neighbour of corrupted-modality harm.

title: Confidence-Aware Fusion via Dempster–Shafer (CMPD)
contribution: Per-modality confidence subnetworks combined evidentially for pedestrian detection.
notes: In-domain precedent for quality/confidence-weighted RGB-T fusion.

title: ProbEn
authors: Chen, Shi, Ye, Mertz, Ramanan, Kong
contribution: Probabilistic late ensembling; marginalization handles missing modalities natively.
notes: Only verified detection-native missing-modality method; KAIST + FLIR.

title: MoME: Resilient Sensor Fusion via Multi-Modal Expert Fusion
contribution: Per-query routing among camera/LiDAR/fused experts by local feature quality.
notes: Strongest analogue of region-dependent takeover (routing, not correction; 3D driving).

title: MEFormer
contribution: Defines and mitigates "negative fusion" from defective modalities.
notes: Names the manuscript's core phenomenon; cite the term.

title: Multimodal Fusion on Low-quality Data: A Comprehensive Survey
contribution: Taxonomy separating noisy, incomplete, imbalanced, quality-varying multimodal data.
notes: Cleanest citation legitimizing the corrupted ≠ missing distinction.

title: DynMM
contribution: On-the-fly gating over modality and fusion-level computation paths.
notes: Dynamic-fusion precedent (efficiency-motivated).

title: Provable Dynamic Fusion for Low-Quality Multimodal Data (QMF)
contribution: Energy-based uncertainty drives dynamic decision-level fusion weights, with guarantees.
notes: Reference quality-aware fusion method; classification-only contrast to feature correction.

title: Trusted Multi-View Classification (TMC)
contribution: Evidential per-view quality assessment with Dempster–Shafer fusion.
notes: Foundational trusted/quality-aware fusion citation.

title: SB-BEVFusion
contribution: BEV fusion explicitly treating corrupted vs missing sensors as distinct cases.
notes: Verbatim corrupted-vs-missing distinction; very recent, camera-LiDAR.

title: MultiCorrupt
contribution: 10 LiDAR-camera corruptions × 3 severities with Resistance Ability metric.
notes: Severity-graded corruption evaluation model.

title: Benchmarking Robustness of 3D Object Detection to Common Corruptions
contribution: 27-corruption benchmark; fusion models more robust, motion corruptions worst.
notes: Corruption-protocol precedent for the manuscript's degradation suite.

title: MM-CKD
contribution: Cross-modal knowledge distillation robust to missing modality (sentiment).
notes: Only distillation-for-missing citation found; non-vision.

title: MMPareto
contribution: Pareto-integrated gradients resolving multimodal/unimodal gradient conflict.
notes: Gradient-conflict framing.

title: Multimodal Learning with Missing Modalities: A Survey
contribution: Survey of imputation/representation/distillation approaches to missing modalities.
notes: Section anchor for Q3.

title: ReconBoost
contribution: Modality-alternating boosting with KL reconcilement vs competition.
notes: Most recent reconcilement-framed balancing method.

title: PMR: Prototypical Modal Rebalance
contribution: Prototypes accelerate the slow-learning modality; entropy regularizer vs dominant modality.
notes: Balancing line representative.

title: ShaSpec
contribution: Shared-specific features + residual fusion for missing modality at train/test.
notes: Representation-side missing-modality approach.

title: OGM-GE
contribution: On-the-fly gradient modulation by modality contribution discrepancy.
notes: Standard balancing citation next to the existing competition papers.

title: SMIL
contribution: Bayesian meta-learning for severely (≤90%) missing modalities.
notes: Canonical missing-modality method citation.

title: Inference-Time Intervention (ITI)
contribution: Shifts selected attention-head activations along probed directions at inference.
notes: Terminological namesake of "intervention"; LLM-only, one clarifying sentence.

title: MEMO
contribution: Per-test-point adaptation via marginal entropy over augmentations.
notes: Single-point test-time intervention precedent.

title: Tent
contribution: Test-time entropy minimization over norm affine parameters.
notes: Canonical "adapt at test time" contrast (parameter-level, unsupervised).

title: OptNet
contribution: Differentiable QP layers via implicit KKT differentiation.
notes: Foundational only; redundant given existing Amos/CF-OPT citations.

title: Visible-Thermal Tiny Object Detection: A Benchmark Dataset and Baselines (RGBT-Tiny)
contribution: RGBT-Tiny benchmark: 115 paired sequences, 93K frames, 1.2M annotations in 7 categories (over 81% of objects under 16x16 px), plus the SAFit evaluation measure and extensive baseline evaluations.
notes: The standard tiny-object RGBT benchmark; also a datasets.md entry.

title: SuperYOLO: Super Resolution Assisted Object Detection in Multimodal Remote Sensing Imagery
contribution: Pixel-level multimodal fusion inside a YOLOv5-style detector plus a super-resolution auxiliary branch (removed at inference) to recover small-object detail.
notes: One of the most-cited YOLO-family multispectral detectors (VEDAI); a detection-native pixel-level entry.

title: Cross-Modality Interactive Attention Network for Multispectral Pedestrian Detection (CIAN)
contribution: Interactive attention module encoding inter-modality correlations to recalibrate channel responses of halfway features before fusion.
notes: Early, heavily cited cross-modal attention design that predates and motivates the transformer fusion line.

title: Guided Attentive Feature Fusion for Multispectral Pedestrian Detection (GAFF)
contribution: Inter- and intra-modality attention modules dynamically weigh and fuse multispectral features at low computational cost.
notes: A widely used comparison point in CFT-era papers; an efficiency-conscious attention baseline.

title: Improving RGB-Infrared Object Detection with Cascade Alignment-Guided Transformer (CAGT)
contribution: Cascades region alignment (TSRA-style) with a complementary fusion transformer inside an RoI detection head; evaluated on DroneVehicle and KAIST.
notes: Transformer-era successor to TSFADet and a sibling of C2Former; strengthens the alignment-aware cluster.

title: Multispectral Deep Neural Networks for Pedestrian Detection (Halfway Fusion)
contribution: Systematically compared early / late / halfway fusion in a two-branch Faster R-CNN and showed mid-level (halfway) fusion works best on KAIST.
notes: The founding deep-learning baseline of the KAIST era; nearly every later pedestrian paper benchmarks against it.

title: Multispectral Pedestrian Detection via Simultaneous Detection and Segmentation (MSDS-RCNN)
contribution: Two-stage multispectral R-CNN jointly optimising detection and semantic segmentation, with a sanitised re-annotation of KAIST training data.
notes: A standard KAIST-era strong baseline; its sanitised annotations are still used by later work.

title: Weakly Aligned Cross-Modal Learning for Multispectral Pedestrian Detection (AR-CNN)
contribution: Region Feature Alignment module predicting and correcting per-modality position shifts inside Faster R-CNN, with RoI jitter training on per-modality annotations.
notes: The reference work for the misalignment problem in pedestrian detection.

title: MLPD: Multi-Label Pedestrian Detector in Multispectral Domain
contribution: Multi-label learning with modality-specific (non-paired) box annotations, so RGB and thermal labels need not coincide — enables training on unpaired multispectral data.
notes: The supervision-side answer to label misalignment, complementing AR-CNN's feature-side alignment.

title: BAANet: Learning Bi-Directional Adaptive Attention Gates for Multispectral Pedestrian Detection
contribution: Bi-directional adaptive attention gates progressively distil modality-specific noise and recalibrate both streams, with illumination-based weighting of interaction strength.
notes: A strong, fast KAIST baseline from the attention-gate family.

title: Learning a Dynamic Cross-Modal Network for Multispectral Pedestrian Detection (DCMNet)
contribution: Dynamically aggregates local and non-local cross-modal context when fusing the streams, instead of a fixed fusion rule.
notes: The main dynamic-fusion representative in pedestrian detection.

title: Translation, Scale and Rotation: Cross-Modal Alignment Meets RGB-Infrared Vehicle Detection (TSFADet)
contribution: TSRA module calibrating feature maps for translation, scale and rotation deviations between modalities, plus a modality-selection strategy, in a two-stream detector for DroneVehicle.
notes: The reference alignment paper for aerial RGBT, where weak misalignment (position/size/angle) is the defining problem.

title: TFDet: Target-Aware Fusion for RGB-T Pedestrian Detection
contribution: Fusion-then-refinement with a segmentation branch and a correlation-maximum loss enhancing pedestrian/background feature contrast to suppress false positives.
notes: Recent SOTA-level results on KAIST, LLVIP, FLIR and M3FD — doubles as a general-detection entry.

title: Weakly Aligned Feature Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection
contribution: Journal extension of the AR-CNN line: weakly aligned feature fusion generalised from pedestrian detection to multimodal object detection.
notes: Bridges pedestrian alignment work and general detection. Early access 2021; issue (vol. 36) published 2025 per Crossref.

title: Fusion of Multispectral Data Through Illumination-Aware Deep Neural Networks for Pedestrian Detection (IATDNN)
contribution: Illumination-aware weighting mechanism modulating a two-stream CNN, trained multi-task with semantic segmentation.
notes: With the illumination-aware Faster R-CNN it defines the day/night adaptive-weighting line that quality-aware methods still cite.

title: Improving Multispectral Pedestrian Detection by Addressing Modality Imbalance Problems (MBNet)
contribution: Differential Modality Aware Fusion plus an illumination-aware feature alignment module, explicitly framed around the modality-imbalance problem in two-stream optimisation.
notes: The named origin of 'modality imbalance' as a pedestrian-detection problem.

title: Drone-Based RGB-Infrared Cross-Modality Vehicle Detection via Uncertainty-Aware Learning (UA-CMDet)
contribution: Introduces the DroneVehicle dataset (28,439 RGB-IR pairs) and weights cross-modal learning by per-object uncertainty from cross-modal IoU and illumination, with illumination-aware NMS.
notes: The aerial anchor paper: DroneVehicle is the standard aerial RGBT benchmark and this is its source paper.

title: Removal and Selection: Improving RGB-Infrared Object Detection via Coarse-to-Fine Fusion
contribution: Coarse-to-fine fusion: first remove modality noise/redundancy from features, then select complementary cross-modal information.
notes: A recent general RGB-IR detection paper framing fusion as noise removal + selection — a clean modern representative of the quality/conflict-aware line.

title: Illumination-Aware Faster R-CNN for Robust Multispectral Pedestrian Detection
contribution: Estimates scene illumination and uses it as a gate to adaptively weight the RGB and thermal sub-networks' detection scores.
notes: The canonical illumination-gated late-fusion design; anchors the decision-level end of the taxonomy.
